children: It looks less likely that aspiring uranium miner Deep Yellow can fully fund a final investment decision on its Tumas project in 4Q, given the current state of the equities market, says Macquarie. "Even if this were possible, the dilution from these share price levels would be excessive," Macquarie says. It thinks a delay is justified to preserve long-term value. Such a move would likely be taken positively by the market, Macquarie adds. It has an "outperform" call on Deep Yellow, and trims its price target by 2.5%, to A$1.95/share. Deep Yellow ended Wednesday at A$0.865, its lowest level since April 2025. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
